$comment: Coverage inventory for the E2E harness. Read by e2e/check-coverage.mjs,
which fails if this file and the code disagree, if a shared spec stops
running on one of the two entrypoints, or if a retired file comes back.
The `ids` lists are generated from the code:
rewrites them and leaves everything else alone. Review the diff. The
`platforms` and `covers` ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â a new suite needs one of these blocks by hand.
`key` is the suite's stable handle and must be unique WITHIN its file.
`cat` is the log category and is NOT unique: SOUND covers three separate
suites in each entrypoint (add / edit / delete).
`platforms` is deliberately asserted, not derived: the checker compares it
against where the code really runs the suite, so a spec quietly wired to
one entrypoint cannot pass by having its manifest edited to match.
A spec is SHARED only if it lives in e2e/specs/ and is both imported and
passed to runSpecs() by e2e-full.mjs (web + win) and e2e-mobile.mjs
(android). Anything platform-specific belongs inline in its entrypoint.
$featuresComment: Every shipped capability the app has. This is what answers 'will my new
feature end up in the tests?' Ã¢â‚¬â€ a `shipped` feature with an empty
`coveredBy` FAILS the checker, so you cannot mark something done without
either tests or an explicit `gap` reason. That is the whole point: the
suite registry alone only enforces that coverage cannot rot, never that
status: `shipped` = implemented in the app, so it MUST be covered.
`planned` = spec written, not implemented, so it need not be.
gap:    an optional reason a `shipped` feature is knowingly uncovered.
Reported on every run, not a silent pass.
coveredBy: suite refs as `<file>::<key>`. A missing ref is an error.

suites.note: PROFILE_SYNC_SPEC.md step 8. The engine is reached by importing /src/profileBundle.js - the same module URL the app imported, so it is the live instance - which only the Vite DEV server serves; the web phase runs a built dist under vite preview, and export/import is Tauri-only by design (§7), so the web arm is I1 and I2 alone. THE NATIVE PICKER IS NEVER STUBBED AND NEVER OPENED, because it cannot be: every property on window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__ is writable:false/configurable:false, and the one writable seam (chrome.webview.postMessage) is bypassed because Tauri's injected ipc captures it in a closure - both measured 2026-10-14. The spec therefore drives everything below the picker, running the app's own destination sequence against a path the test names; only the picker's two-line handoff is left to the user's hand-test. Clicking Export/Import here would open a #32770 that wedges the run. I0 logs ONLY when the spec's try/catch contains an exception, which is a real failure - it exists so a throw cannot unwind main() and skip the entrypoint's localStorage restore. Skipped ids print a SKIP line rather than logging a WARN, which would push the web phase off its exit-0 baseline. Runs after profiles (F) and before refcount (G) and reset (O), which re-seed for themselves
